title: Change request
description: One unit of work put to an agent, against the pinned target application. The statement is what an arm renders for the agent; the invariants and the acceptance checks are ground truth the agent never sees, applied by the harness after the run.

category.description: The four kinds of work the change-request set covers.

modules.description: The modules of the target application the change may touch, first the one it principally belongs to. A cross-service change names more than one; the harness runs each module's suite and places each hidden check in the module that declares it.

difficulty.description: What makes this change request hard, from the taxonomy the pilot's ceiling effect made necessary. `single_endpoint` is the easy shape the pilot used and is kept only where a category needs a floor.

difficulty_rationale.description: Why this change request is expected to separate the arms: what the easy path is, and what it costs the agent that takes it.

needs_stack.description: Whether verifying this change request needs the application running. Module tests do not; anything that exercises a service over the wire does. Defaults to false.

statement.description: What is being asked for, and the observable behaviour that settles it. This is the only part an arm may render for the agent.

context.description: Background an arm may also render: where the behaviour lives, what prompted the request.

behaviours.description: The observable outcomes that settle the request, one per item. Visible to every arm: this is the content the arms represent differently, so it must be the same content in each. It is a decomposition of the statement, not additional information, and it never restates a hidden check.

boundaries.description: Boundaries the request states openly, as any well-written change request would. Distinct from must_invariants: these are told to the agent, those are how the harness scores it. Their substance may overlap; the harness never takes the agent's word for either.

must_invariants.description: Boundaries the change must not cross. Violating one means the change is not a success, however green its acceptance checks.

acceptance.description: Hidden tests. They live in bench/, are never placed in the workspace or the prompt, and are run by the harness after the agent has finished.

evidence.description: Runtime evidence captured from the pinned application, carried into the change request as input. Every arm renders it and the agent reads it; nothing in it names a hidden check or an invariant. Captured by infra/capture_evidence.py against the running pin, never written by hand, so it cannot drift from what the application actually does. Required for an incident, whose whole premise is something that was observed.

summary.description: What the evidence shows, in one or two sentences.

path.description: The artifact's home, relative to the repository root. Tracked openly and placed in the agent's workspace.

paths.description: Paths relative to the target application root.

module.description: The module this check is placed in and run from. Must be one the change request names.

source.description: The test's home, relative to the repository root. Tracked openly here; hidden from the agent.

destination.description: Where the harness places it in the workspace, relative to the target application root.
